title: Conditional generative models
description: A conditional generative model p(x|c) can be obtained by adding c as input to both the generator and discriminator; the authors propose this as a straightforward extension.
canonical_description: conditional generative modeling by conditioning generator and discriminator

evidence.quote: \item A { conditional generative} model $p(\bm{x} \mid \bm{c})$ can be obtained by adding $\bm{c}$

verdict.reasoning: The gap describes the proposal that conditioning a generative model can be achieved by feeding the conditioning variable into both the generator and discriminator. The deep-read paper — Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets — is precisely this contribution. It formally introduces conditioning by feeding y into both the generator and discriminator, states the resulting two-player minimax objective over D(x|y) and G(z|y), and validates the construction empirically on class-conditioned MNIST digits and MIR Flickr image-tag generation. The limitations noted in the assessment (proof-of-concept accuracy on MNIST, preliminary multi-modal results, single-tag conditioning, and joint language-model training left to future work) concern the maturity and breadth of results, not the gap's specific mechanism. Since the proposed extension is directly formalized and demonstrated, the gap is fully addressed. Confidence is high because the evidence squarely matches the gap's exact statement, though it rests on a single paper and the empirical results are acknowledged as preliminary.

paper.title: Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets
paper.abstract: Generative Adversarial Nets [8] were recently introduced as a novel way to train generative models. In this work we introduce the conditional version of generative adversarial nets, which can be constructed by simply feeding the data, y, we wish to condition on to both the generator and discriminator. We show that this model can generate MNIST digits conditioned on class labels. We also illustrate how this model could be used to learn a multi-modal model, and provide preliminary examples of an application to image tagging in which we demonstrate how this approach can generate descriptive tags which are not part of training labels.

assessments.contribution_summary: This paper is precisely the work that proposed the extension described in the gap: it introduces conditional generative adversarial nets by feeding the conditioning variable y into both the generator and the discriminator, and formalizes the resulting two-player minimax objective (D(x|y), G(z|y)). It implements and demonstrates the idea with experiments on MNIST digit generation conditioned on class labels and on MIR Flickr image-tag generation for multi-modal modeling.
assessments.what_remains_open: The gap's specific problem — proposing and validating that conditioning c can be added as input to both generator and discriminator to obtain a conditional generative model — is fully addressed by this paper, which even demonstrates the construction empirically. What the paper itself leaves open is not the proposed mechanism but rather its efficacy and maturity: the authors state the MNIST results are a "proof-of-concept" that are outperformed by several other approaches including non-conditional adversarial nets, the multi-modal tag-generation results are preliminary, tags are used only individually rather than jointly, and joint training of the language model is left to future work. These are refinements beyond the gap's stated scope.
evidence_snippets: Generative adversarial nets can be extended to a conditional model if both the generator and discriminator are conditioned on some extra information ${\bm{y}}$.
We can perform the conditioning by feeding ${\bm{y}}$ into the both the discriminator and generator as additional input layer.

In this work we introduce the conditional version of generative adversarial nets, which can be constructed by simply feeding the data, ${y}$, we wish to condition on to both the generator and discriminator.
